title: Laser-cut MDF side panel with slots and cut-outs
prompt: Side panel for a box I'm laser cutting from 3 mm MDF, 120 x 80 mm. Along the bottom it needs two 15 x 3.2 mm slots for the bottom panel's tabs, their centres 6 mm up from the bottom edge and 30 mm either side of the middle. Four M3 holes (3.4 mm) 5 mm in from the edges at each corner. Then, all 45 mm up from the bottom: an 8 mm hole for a DC barrel jack 30 mm from the left edge, a 12 mm hole for a toggle switch in the middle, and a 12 x 11 mm rectangular cut-out (12 wide) for a USB-B socket centred 30 mm from the right edge.

hidden_tests.description: Evaluates cleanly and every body is a valid closed solid
120 x 80 mm panel, 3 mm thick, ±0.1 mm
Nine openings: 2 slots, 4 screw holes, jack, switch and USB cut-out
Jack 30 mm from the left edge and switch in the middle, both 45 mm up (35 mm from the top)
Four M3 clearance holes (3.2–3.5 mm), each 5 mm in from both edges
Eighteen flat faces: the outline, both rectangular slots, the USB cut-out, front and back

notes: The reference draws the switch hole as two semicircular arcs, the way DXF exports often do; the IR checks count a closed loop of co-circular arcs as one circle. Tab slots are 3.2 wide for 3 mm MDF plus kerf slack.
